test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions I, II and III. Consider the information given in the statements as true, even if it seems to be at variance with commonly known facts, and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements?

**statement:**

All ornaments are decorations.

Some flowers are ornaments.

All plants are flowers.

**The conclusion**

I. All plants are ornaments.

II. Some decorations are ornaments.

III. Some flowers are plants.

options.text: Only conclusion II and III follow
Only conclusion I and II follow
Only conclusion I and III follow

solution:
Given statement:

All ornaments are decorations.

Some flowers are ornaments.

All plants are flowers.

The least possible Venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f581fab6bdcb13ec880df96479e10d694e158c3a6bc31fc2e0d7fcd8edc31ceb.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All plants are ornaments. - **False **(because there is no direct relation given between plants are ornaments. So it can be possible but not definite)

II. Some decorations are ornaments. - True (Because, All ornaments are decorations given. So Some decorations are ornaments it is definite)

III. Some flowers are plants. - True (Because, All plants are flowers given. So Some flowers are plants it is definite)

So, Only conclusion II and III follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Only conclusion II and III follow**".
